summary: Full backend + frontend verification of Crew Bank v3 features (status toggle, post-to-feed opt-in, prominent CREW BANK pill, landing 'Open crew slots' section, modal glitch fixes). 9/9 pytest cases pass sequentially. All UI behaviors verified: modal opens, Escape closes, body scroll locks, inside-click does not close, backdrop click closes (except at very top strip covered by sticky nav — see minor issue), status toggle Found⇄Seeking works with toast, post-to-feed checkbox present, opening a different event's modal shows fresh (non-stale) state. Landing OpenCrewSlots renders 1 card for Race Week Bellingham; free-user 402/premium-user 200 checks green.

ui_bugs.issue: Sticky nav header has z-50 same as modal outer wrapper; at the top ~64px strip the header intercepts backdrop clicks (elementFromPoint(20,20) returns the HEADER, not the modal). Backdrop click works everywhere else. Fix: bump modal z-index to z-[60] (or make the top strip of the modal wrapper cover the header).

action_items: (Optional/minor) Raise CrewBankModal outer z-index above the sticky header (currently both z-50) so the very top strip is a clickable backdrop.
Note: run pytest with -n 0 for this suite — the parallel xdist scheduler causes a race between TestStatusPatch and TestOpenCrewSlots since they mutate the same crew_bank row.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1376 lines — still over the 700-line guideline. Split into modules (events, crew_bank, aggregator_admin, auth, payments, seed).

GET /crew-bank/open — the $expr on event_ends_at compares full ISO ('$ifNull...') to now_iso[:10] ('YYYY-MM-DD'). String comparison works for lexicographic ISO but fragile: 'YYYY-MM-DD' < 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:...' will match when dates are equal, which is what we want (event ending today is still active). Consider normalizing both sides to date strings explicitly for clarity.
CrewBankModal.jsx line 100: outer div uses z-50. MainNav sticky header also uses z-50. DOM order alone determines stacking → header wins at overlap. Prefer z-[60] on modal.

post_to_feed=True writes a post with id 'crew_{event}_{user}' via upsert. Good. But: turning off post_to_feed on a re-join does NOT delete the previously-created post — the community feed post lingers. Consider deleting the post when post_to_feed=false AND the doc exists, or when status flips to 'found'.
seed_data_creation: Temporarily inserted a crew_bank entry for the premium user against Race Week Bellingham to exercise landing OpenCrewSlots + modal-in-pool state; auto-cleaned at end via DELETE /events/{id}/crew and manual mongosh deletion of the linked_crew post.
